title: Add a cross-target check matrix now that the workspace is pure Rust
description:
39d0331 removed ring, and cross-compilation now works from the Linux runner with no extra toolchain. Measured there:
  persona-core -> aarch64-apple-darwin      exit 0
  persona-core -> x86_64-pc-windows-msvc    exit 0
  persona-core -> aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos exit 0
  whole workspace -> aarch64-apple-darwin    exit 0

cargo check runs build scripts but never links, so a plain ubuntu runner needs no cross linker and no extra install step.

This supersedes persona-vvs2.1, which proposed a windows-latest job limited to persona-core. A cross-check matrix is strictly better: it covers every target from one runner, costs no extra runner minutes, and catches Unix-only code entering a crate that is supposed to stay portable — which is the actual failure mode, since persona-core holds the crypto and the pseudonym derivation.

Suggested: a job running cargo check --target <t> -p persona-core for the three targets, plus --workspace for aarch64-apple-darwin. Do NOT add --workspace for Windows: persona-grpc is still Unix-only by design, 21 UnixListener/UnixStream sites, tracked by this epic's parent. Widen per crate as the transport abstraction lands.
close_reason:
Decided by Mark 2026-09-15 (cross-check matrix, not a windows-latest runner) and implemented in 34c4e4a. A 'portability' job on ubuntu-latest runs cargo check --target for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, aarch64-apple-darwin and aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos against persona-core, plus --workspace for darwin. Also added 'make portability', wired into 'make ci', so local and CI cover the same thing.

Bead's measurements re-verified on this machine and all still hold: all four checks exit 0 (0-2s warm). One correction to its claim of 'no extra install step' -- dtolnay/rust-toolchain installs only the host target, so the job needs a 'targets:' line. That is one line, not a step.

ONE PART OF THE BEAD'S ARGUMENT DOES NOT HOLD. It says the matrix 'covers every target from one runner', implying that includes macOS. CI already has a macos-latest leg, which compiles the same #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] arms, so the darwin half adds no coverage CI lacked -- only faster failure and, more usefully, coverage on a developer's Linux box where those arms are never type-checked at all. The matrix's unique CI value is Windows and ohos, which nothing covered.

Both failure modes measured, not assumed:
- std::os::unix MetadataExt added to persona-core (std only, no new dependency, the realistic shape of drift): native cargo check exit 0, windows cross-check exit 101.
- type error inside a #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] arm in persona-grpc: native workspace check exit 0, darwin cross-check exit 101.
A first attempt at the drift mutation used libc, which is not a persona-core dependency, so the native check caught it too and the test proved nothing about the gate; redone with std::os::unix.

Rejected, with reasons: a windows-latest job running cargo test -p persona-core (persona-core's tests are byte-exact arithmetic with no platform-dependent behaviour, so running them on Windows proves ~nothing compiling them does not -- free on this public repo, but thin signal for a second runner's wall-clock on every PR); and doing nothing until the transport abstraction lands (accepts silent drift in the crate holding the crypto).
